description_en: Thehitihas a 5th century statue of Akṣobhya.  Ālko Hiti is operated by the community. Writing of Ikhāchẽ Ṭola in hisKīrtipatākā(verse 34) in NS 772 (1652 CE), Kunu Śarmā, the court poet of King Śrīnivāsa Malla, mentions thishitiby referring to a stone spout at the north of theṭola.There are five stone spouts in the Hiti, of which three face south, one faces west, and the last faces north. Statues of Buddhist and Hindu deities including Licchavi caityas, Buddha statues from the Licchavi period, and the Śikharakūṭa temple of Nārāyaṇa have been erected in and around the Hiti precinct.This Hiti was established by Tuhūdeva Vajrācārya together with his wives Indralakṣmī and Jayalakṣmī, son Phyakudeva and daughter Śuṃdaralakṣmī on Thursday 8th of the bright fortnight of NS 535 (1415 CE). Since it was the dry season, the Hiti was constructed after the performance of a Tantric ritual. It seems that the Licchavi Caitya was established here even before the establishment of the Hiti. Similarly, the inscription from 533 BCE (1413 CE), which was erected in the Hiti area suggests that cultural activities took place here even before the watering site was constructed.When the sons of Tuhūdeva divided their properties, the three brothers inherited three different monuments. One received Ānā Bāhāḥ (LAL0980) and its land, the other Ālko Hiti and its land, and the last one the Āgama deity and its land. The descendants of the son who received Ālko Hiti are still running the site, and Tusiṃ Vajracharya, a descendant of Tuhūdeva, is currently the one taking care of it.Some locals tell the following legend about the establishment of the Hiti. One day when Tuhūdeva went to work in his field, a serpent-king (Nāgarāja) disguised as a man came to meet him. The man told Tuhūdeva he must treat his wife as she had a problem with her eyes. Tuhūdeva knew which medicine to get, so he went with the serpent and made a treatment for his wife. The King became very happy and told Tuhūdeva to ask him for a gift. As Tuhūdeva was a prosperous and generous man, he did not ask for wealth but instead asked for the welfare of people. Pleased, Nāgarāja gave him five pebbles and told him to hide them somewhere until an auspicious time. Tuhūdeva hid the stones in a box and placed it with his treasure. One day, his wife opened the box. She thought that the pebbles were useless and threw them away. The stones fell in five places and the five water fountains burst open. When Tuhūdeva came home from his work, he found out that his wife had thrown the stones away. He became upset and scolded his wife. Afterwards, he made stone spouts in the place where the water had burst from the earth.A copperplate inscription describing the establishment of the Hiti contains a regulation that instructs readers how to perform the anniversary worship of the Hiti. Nowadays, however, this ritual no longer takes place. Every year on the 1st day of Vaiśākha, Tusiṃ Vajracharya, a descendant of Tuhūdeva, worships the Hiti. On the day of Sithinakhaḥ, he cleans the water place and worships the spouts, and on the day of Indrajātrā (13th day of the bright fortnight of Bhādra) a tableau presenting the biography of Buddha is displayed in the Hiti. At present, a committee of the site's stakeholders has been formed. This committee has managed to collect the water in a big tank to be distributed to locals via pipes. Earlier, water used to flow from all the spouts of the Hiti all year round, but increasing urbanisation has caused the groundwater level to decrease. This means that many streams now dry up in the dry season. However, water begins to flow from the spouts again when the rainy season starts.
description_ne: ललितपुरमा रहेका ढुंगेधाराहरूमध्ये समुदायको तर्फबाट व्यवस्थित रूपले संचालन भइरहेको नमूना ढुंगेधारा आल्को हिति हो । राजा श्रीनिवास मल्लका दरबारिया कवि कुनु शर्माले नेसं ७७२ मा लेखेकोकीर्तिपताका(श्लोक ३४) मा इखाछेँ टोलको वर्णन गर्दा टोलको उत्तरतिर ढुंगेधारा (प्रणाली) रहेको उल्लेख गरेका छन् । कुनु शर्माले वर्णन गरेको ढुंगेधारा यही हुनुपर्छ । यस हितिमा पाँचवटा टुटीहरू रहेका छन् । ती पाँचवटा टुटीमध्ये तीनवटा दक्षिणाभिमुख, एउटा पश्चिमाभिमुख र एउटा उत्तराभिमिख गरी बनाइएको छ । हिति प्राङ्गण र हिति वरिपरि लिच्छवि चैत्यहरू, लिच्छविकालीन बुद्ध मूर्ति, नारायणको शिखरकूट मन्दिर लगायत बौद्ध र हिन्दू देवीदेवताका मूर्तिहरू स्थापना गरिएका छन् ।यो हिति तुहूदेव वज्राचार्यले नेसं ५३५ फागुण शुक्ल ८ विहिवारको दिनमा आफ्ना दुई श्रीमतीहरू इन्द्रलक्ष्मी र जयलक्ष्मी, छोरा फ्यकुदेव र छोरी शुंदरलक्ष्मी सहित भई यो ढुंगेधारा स्थापना गरेका थिए । त्यस वेला जलवृष्टि नभई सुख्खा परेकोले तान्त्रिक विधिबाट नवनाग साधना गरी ढुंगेधारा स्थापना गरिएको थियो । यस ठाउँमा हिति स्थापना हुनुभन्दा अगाडिदेखि नै लिच्छवि चैत्य स्थापना भइसकेको देखिन्छ । त्यस्तै हिति स्थापना हुनुभन्दा अघिको नेसं ५३३ को शिलापत्र पनि प्राप्त भएबाट हिति बन्नुभन्दा अघि नै यो ठाउँमा सांस्कृतिक गतिविधि चलिसकेको प्रमाणित हुन्छ ।तुहूदेवका सन्ततिहरूको अंशबण्डा हुँदा तीनजना दाजुभाइको भागमा तीनवटा अलग-अलग सम्पदा परेका थिए । एकजनाको भागमा आन बाहा: र त्यसको जग्गा, एकजनाको भागमा आल्को हिति र त्यसको जग्गा, एकजनाको भागमा आगम देवता र त्यसको जग्गा परेको थियो । जसको भागमा आल्को हिति परेको थियो उनका सन्ततिहरूले यस हितिको रेखदेख गर्दैआइरहेका छन् । अहिले तुहूदेवका सन्तति तुसिं वज्राचार्यले हितिको संरक्षक भई काम गरिरहेका छन् ।यो हितिको निर्माणसम्बन्धी एउटा किंवदन्ती रहेको छ । एक दिन तुहूदेव वज्राचार्य आफ्नो खेतमा काम गर्न जाँदा नागराज मानिसको रूप धारण गरी तुहूदेवलाई भेट्न आए । उनले आफ्नी श्रीमतीको आँखा दुखी अति कष्ट भएको हुँदा तुहूदेवलाई उपचार गरिदिन आग्रह गरे । तुहूदेवले वैद्य काम पनि जानेका थिए त्यसैले नागराजसँग गई उनले नागिनीको आँखाको उपचार गरिदिए । नागराजले खुशी हुँदै तुहूदेवलाई वरदान माग्न भने । तुहूदेव सम्पन्न र उदार व्यक्ति भएको हुँदा धनसम्पत्ति नमागीकन जगत उद्धार हुने वरदान मागेका थिए । नागराजले प्रसन्न भई पाँचवटा ढुंगा (Pebbles) दिई कसैलाई नदेखाई लुकाइराख्नू र शुभ साइतमा मात्र निकाल्नू भनी पठाए । तुहूदेवले पनि ती ढुंगाहरू कसैलाई नदेखाई आफ्नो ढुकुटीमा लगी सन्दूकभित्र लुकाइराखे । एक दिन तुहूदेवकी श्रीमतीले सन्दूक खोली हेर्दा पाँचवटा ढुंगा मात्र देखेपछि यस्तो ढुंगा पनि सन्दूकभित्र राख्ने हो र भनी फ्याँकीदिइन् । ती ढुंगाहरू पाँच ठाउँमा पर्न गई पानीको मूल फुट्यो । तुहूदेव कामबाट फर्केर घर आउँदा नागराजले दिएका ढुंगाहरू श्रीमतीले मिल्काएको थाहा भयो । उनले दिक्क भई श्रीमतीलाई गाली गरे । तैपनि उनले पानीको मूल फुटेको ठाउँमा ढुंगेधारा बनाई व्यवस्थित गरिदिए ।हिति स्थापनासम्बन्धी लेखिएको ताम्रपत्रमा हितिको वर्षबन्धन गर्नुपर्ने नियम बनाइएको छ, तर अहिले हितिको वर्षबन्धन गरिँदैन । प्रत्येक वर्ष वैशाख १ गते तुहूदेवका सन्तति तुसिं वज्राचार्यले हितिको पूजा गरिरहेका छन् । सिथिनख:को दिनमा हिति सफा गरिन्छ र तुसिं वज्राचार्यले नै हितिको पनि पूजा गर्छन् । प्रत्येक वर्ष भाद्र शुक्ल १३ (इन्द्रजात्रा) को दिनमा हितिगा:मा बुद्धको जीवनीसँग सम्बन्धित झाँकी प्रदर्शन गरिन्छ । अहिले आल्को हिति संरक्षण तथा उपभोक्ता समिति गठन गरी राति प्रयोगविहीन भई बगिरहने पानीलाई ठूलो ट्यांकीमा जम्मा गरी पाइपमार्फत् घरघरमा वितरण गर्ने कार्य भइरहेको छ । पहिले हितिका सबै धाराबाट बाह्रै महिना पानी बगिरहन्थ्यो तर अहिले बढ्दो शहरीकरणले गर्दा जमिनमुनि पानीको सतह घट्दै गएकोले सुख्खा याममा धारा सुक्न थालेको छ, तर पनि वर्षा याममा पानी पर्न थालेपछि हितिबाट फेरि पानी झर्न थाल्दछ ।

historical_events.event_description: Śaṅkarasiṃha restored thehitiduṃ(a wooden structure with functions such as underground pipes to channel water from the source to the Hiti).
During the reign of King Mahendra Śāha, the Hiti was restored by collecting donations.
Āloka Hiti Saṃrakṣaṇa Tathā Khānepānī Vikāsa Upasamiti (Ālok Hiti Conservation and Water Supply Users’ Committee) renovated the Hiti premises, including the surrounding walls and the water source.

Together with his wives Indralakṣmī and Jayalakṣmī, his son Phyakudeva and his daughter Śuṃdaralakṣmī, Tuhūdeva Vajrācārya had this Hiti constructed on Thursday 8thof the bright fortnight of NS 535 (1415 CE). Since it was dry at the time, a Tantric ritual was performed in advance of its construction. He also bestowed nineropanīsof land upon the Hiti to fund its continued maintenance. The copperplate regulates that the stone which was placed after the Tantric ritual should never be uncovered. In addition to this, honey, dirts, soap and leather shoes should not be taken into the Hiti area.The copperplate mentions that there is a stone inscription attached to the Caitya, and that this provides more information about the construction of the Hiti. However, this inscription is missing.
An inscription dated 1413 CE was erected in the area before the construction of the spouts. It could not be figured out what Ajay Bharo did on this date.

After the bone factory closed in VS 2057, locals became more conscious of the need to conserve and protect the monument. The stakeholders formed a committee named Ālko Hiti Saṃrakṣaṇa Tathā Khānepānī Vikāsa Upasamiti (Ālko Hiti Conservation and Water Supply Users’ Committee). The committee has now managed to collect the water in a big tank so that it can be distributed to locals via pipes. The committee collected Rs. 2,000 from every household to raise funds for the construction of this system.

A factory producing manure from buffalo bones was established to the east of the Hiti. After heavy rains, the water from the bones collected in the factory mixed with the water for the Hiti, and bloody water started to flow from the spouts. The administration closed the bone factory after locals protested.
